translation:
Harishran Jagmohanbhai writes about Puniyad:

_Mathura chhodi Shyam aaviya, haanre ene vaas kidho Puniyad dhaamma_ (Leaving Mathura, Shyam [Krishna] came and made his home in the divine abode of Puniyad.)

Shri Dham Puniyad is the place where all the saints abide in the abode of happiness, and where Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj is seated. O Lord of Grace, you have come to lift souls out of the ocean of worldly existence (bhavsagar).

Puniyad is located in Vadodara district, 2 km from Bamangam on National Highway 8 out of Por. Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj came from Shahpura and settled in Puniyad, and an account of this is known through oral tradition. As Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj was travelling with his company of saints, singing the praises of Hari, they arrived at Puniyad, where a well was being dug. Jivanji Maharaj saw this and fell into thought; he told the well-diggers to come out at once, for through his foresight he had seen that the well was about to collapse. By the power of his word, no sooner had the labourers climbed out than the well caved in with a crash.

As this news spread through the village, the village elders and leaders came, and they were filled with reverence for the saints. They made this request to Jivanji Maharaj: "See how you have saved us from being buried in the well - so stay here and save us from the well of worldly existence (bhavkoop) too. Holy company (satsang) is the root of all good fortune - that is our heartfelt wish," they said. "Maharaj, we have heard that the dry peepal tree of Dhanora turned green, and we were coming to have your darshan (sacred sight). We have also learned, O Maharaj, that it is true you gave new life to Harmabai, who was disabled from birth, and removed her disability. Harmabai has resolved in mind, deed, and word to wed herself to you, and you graciously accepted, saying that at present you hold the state of a sadhu (renunciate) and must go on pilgrimage, but that in future you would fulfil her wish - this promise you gave. If this is true, then knowing our wish, accept what is in our hearts. It is our wish that you, together with Harmaba and the saints, come and settle in our village."

Sadguru Jivandas said, "As the merciful Lord wills. When we return from pilgrimage we will try to fulfil your wish. There must be some unfinished bond (lenden) between us and this land." Signs from beyond (agam) were felt that in time to come, so that the devotional longing of the saints might be fulfilled, this sacred land would become an abode of devotion (bhaktidham). Saying "Ramkabir" to all, they then set out from there on pilgrimage.

Whatever the feelings in Harmaba's heart, and whatever reverence the villagers held for Sadguru Jivanji, it is recorded in the genealogist's (vahivancha) register that in Samvat 1730 Jivanji settled in Puniyad. Puna means "again" and yaad means "remembrance" - such may be the meaning of the name Puniyad: just as, on the peak of Kaleshwar (Kailash), the kunj bird never forgets to care for its young, so too, as if a remembrance came to him of caring for his own children (baalgopal, his devotees), he settled in Puniyad, and toward the end declared:

_Tahaan Ayodhya jahaan Raghupati, Kahanad tahaan Gokul gaam, Saptapuri tahaan Jeevana, jahaan santsangat Harinaam._ (Wherever Raghupati [Ram] is, there is Ayodhya; wherever Kahan [Krishna] is, there is the village of Gokul; wherever Jeevana [Jivanji] is, there is one of the seven sacred cities [Saptapuri] - wherever the company of saints chants the name of Hari.)

Hearing such words from his own devotees, he agreed to keep the garden (vaadi) of Puniyad. Until now, eleven generations of Jivanji Maharaj's lineage have held this seat (gadi). In Puniyad, the abode of loving devotion, worship of the seat (gadi puja) is performed in his own temple. On the seat, the relic of Jivanji Maharaj's presence (samagam), Jivanji Maharaj's own prayer beads (mala), and the quilt (godadi) that Jivanji Maharaj used when he appeared in the form of Narsinhdas at the time of Narsinhdas's calamity and cured the Suba's leprosy, are all worshipped.

This is the original seat (mool gadi) of the Uda devotees, established through Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj.
